correctness.rationale: The proof begins with h(j)=1-Mf(j)=min_r |B_r(j)∩Z|/|B_r(j)|, so h vanishes on one-vertices and lies in (0,m/n] on zero-vertices. A boundary zero pair has identical heights because balls centered at positions 1 and 2 include the same potentially maximizing prefixes, while the only missing prefixes are all-zero. Every singleton zero run contributes b_R h, an interior zero pair contributes a+|a-b|+b=2max(a,b), and boundary pairs contribute one height; since runs are separated by one-vertices these sum with no overlap, proving the exact nonnegative defect and bound for arbitrary n≥3. The ball-density equality condition follows from H_R=m/n, and a single zero realizes it for every n. The isolated three-zero example is only a failure of the local two-height decomposition, not a counterexample to the unproved unrestricted conjecture. Independent exact-rational centered-ball computation checked all 2014 admissible nonconstant words for n=3..11, including 269 equalities and boundary pairs; no finite check is claimed as a proof of all n.
